name: textascii
algorithm: One std.text function (graphemes, width, Nfc normalization, full case folding), reps passes over mostly-ASCII text generated in the program from splitmix64(seed), mib MiB, 6 of 256 scalars outside ASCII (README.md). Mk only: no std among C, Rust, Zig and Go has grapheme segmentation, width, normalization or full case folding; the row also serves tools/bench compare of the ASCII fast paths before and after.

skip.c: no std Unicode segmentation, normalization, case folding or width: C has none
skip.rust: no std Unicode segmentation, normalization, case folding or width in Rust (unicode-segmentation, unicode-normalization and unicode-width are crates; no crate stands in)
skip.zig: no std Unicode segmentation, normalization, case folding or width in Zig (std.unicode has UTF-8 and UTF-16 only)
skip.go: no std Unicode segmentation, normalization, full case folding or width in Go (golang.org/x/text and rivo/uniseg are not std)
skip.mk-wrap: the checksum already uses the wrapping operators

no_counts: B24 does not apply: a Mk-only row (no other std has the facility)
notes: The text is at least 16 MiB: of 256 draws, 180 a lower-case letter (an upper-case one in seven), 36 a space, 14 a digit, 16 ASCII punctuation, 4 a newline, and 6 one non-ASCII scalar each: a Latin-1 letter from U+00C0 (most decompose), Cyrillic, CJK, an emoji, a Latin-1 letter from U+00E0, a combining mark from U+0300. tests/bench-lanes/std-text2/unicode is the same functions on text with 6 of 16 scalars outside ASCII.
